label: FAO 2014, Genebank Standards for Plant Genetic Resources for Food and Agriculture
notes: 9.6 MB full PDF. THE authoritative definition of ideal storage. Long-term base collection: -18 +/- 3 C at 15 +/- 3 pct RH, hermetically sealed. Medium-term active collection: 5-10 C at 15 +/- 3 pct RH. Drying to equilibrium at 5-20 C and 10-25 pct RH. Note the standard is written in equilibrium RH, NOT moisture content.

label: FAO, Practical guide for the application of the Genebank Standards
notes: 3.7 MB PDF. Operational companion to the 2014 standards.

label: Groot et al. 2025 - Modelling the quantitative effect of oxygen on the ageing of primed celery seeds
notes: The Plant Journal 2025. PMC12005833 free full text used because Wiley returned 403. THE source for the oxygen multiplier. 96 treatment combinations: 4 temps (5/13/20/30 C) x 4 RH (16/33/43/60 pct) x 6 O2 levels (1/5.2/10/21/50/99 pct), up to 7 years. Log-log linear O2 vs p50. Each halving of O2 gives about +72 pct longevity, INDEPENDENT OF TEMPERATURE. Below 1 pct O2 gives about 11x shelf life. Effect diminishes at 60 pct RH and is absent at 60 pct RH plus 30 C.

label: Rice seed longevity in the context of seed moisture contents and hypoxic conditions
notes: Seed Science Research. Second species line of evidence for the moisture-by-oxygen interaction.

label: Whitehouse et al. 2018 - Genebank standards for drying orthodox seeds may not be optimal
notes: Biopreserv Biobank 16(5):327-336. Full text. Initial high-temperature drying (40-60 C) of freshly harvested seed improves subsequent longevity versus the standard 5-20 C protocol. Evidence that pre-storage history sets a baseline the tool cannot observe. Relevant to K_i, not to the storage multipliers.

label: Solberg et al. 2020 - Long-Term Storage and Longevity of Orthodox Seeds: A Systematic Review
notes: Front Plant Sci 11:1007. Open access full text. Systematic review. States the abiotic factors of greatest importance are HUMIDITY, TEMPERATURE and OXYGEN - light is not among them. Also carries species P50 rankings (long-lived versus short-lived) usable for baseline longevity tiers.

label: Seed Longevity - The Evolution of Knowledge and a Conceptual Framework

notes: Supplied by the user. Full derivation of v = Ki - p/sigma and log10 sigma = KE - CW log10 m - CH t - CQ t^2. Contains two fully worked examples (lettuce and barley at -20 C) that reproduce to the day and are used as regression anchors in viability_equation_anchors.csv.

label: Ellis, R.H. 1991 - The Longevity of Seeds. HortScience 26(9):1119

notes: Supplied by the user; CC BY-NC open access via CentAUR. Seed Sci Technol 50(Suppl.1):1-20. label: Yildirim, Ozturk & Demir 2021 - Vacuum Versus Open Air Storage for Pepper Seed Longevity Over 48 Months
notes: HortiS 38(2):110-115, retrieved via DergiPark. DIRECTLY ANSWERS THE VACUUM-JAR QUESTION at realistic home-storage conditions: 4 pepper cultivars, vacuum-sealed vs perforated cheesecloth, 13 C / 35 percent RH, 48 months, seed MC 7.1-7.6 percent. Vacuum was significantly better for ALL cultivars at 48 months but the difference was NOT significant before 36 months (except cv. Yaglik from 24 months). Oil and reducing-sugar loss were both faster in open air. Also gives an eRH-to-MC anchor: pepper equilibrates to about 7.1-7.3 percent MC at 35-50 percent RH and 13-17 C.
